buyer: European Commission, DG REGIO - Regional and Urban Policy
title: Belgium – Business and management consultancy and related services – Learning through Experimentation for Adaptive Programming (LEAP) - Producing experimental designs for ERDF/CF/JTF investment in the field of access to quality public services
description: The overarching goal of this assignment is to prepare the ground for embedding experimentation in National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs) from the outset of the 2028–2034 programming period. To this end, the assignment will structurally bring evaluators and programmers to work together, build capacity on both sides, and provide the EU evaluation system with practical experimentation tools that extend beyond the three participating MS. This assignment focuses on investments on access to public services and shall produce the following outputs: 1. NRPP-ready experimental designs to be implemented in the 2028–2034 programming period in three Member States; 2. a detailed toolkit to support MS in the introduction of experimental designs in 2028-2034 Plans: LEAP Kit (Learning through Experimentation for Adaptive Programming). Access to quality public services is central to the Right to Stay initiative and to the social and territorial cohesion objectives of the EU. Ensuring that services remain within reach of citizens, particularly in lagging and rural regions, is increasingly challenging as budgets tighten and demographic pressures intensify. The constraint is often not only that infrastructure is missing or outdated, but its accessibility and quality is not up to standards. The question of intervention approaches in this regard is underexplored and poorly evidenced. Experimentation through randomised controlled trials (RCTs) - and the analysis of experiment results to identify the causal effects of interventions - offers the most rigorous way to generate this evidence. Improving the capacity to design and conduct experimental designs is even more important in light of the evolving regulatory context. The Commission proposal for the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework explicitly promotes policy learning and experimentation as a function of both coordinating and managing authorities (Articles 50 and 51 of the proposed Performance Regulation). DG REGIO’s ambition is that experimental designs and adaptive learning mechanisms will be embedded in the NRPPs from the outset of the next programming period.

This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: TBD - The approximate value of Project will be $50M to $100M. Formal Sources Sought Response Due � before 3:00 pm PDT on 26 November 2026 2. Project Details and Background. The USCG Station at Cape Disappointment requires repairs, upgrades, and improvements to existing infrastructure and nearby areas to restore and retain full mission readiness. The Station is on an unstable sandbar which has experienced sediment migration into dock and adjacent waterway areas. Dock structures are failing and require repair/replacement. The vessel haul-out facility is currently inoperable due to sedimentation and requires the USCG to conduct frequent maintenance dredging. Haul-out structure is failing and requires replacement. Adjacent landscape features pose rockfall dangers above the engineering and maintenance buildings to people and property 3. Project Scope. Rockfall slope instability corrective measures: Anticipated rockfall mitigation will require corrective measures including but not limited to tree removal, rock scaling, rock dowel installation, draped mesh removal and replacement, removal and/or repair of an existing damaged ringnet fence, and installation of a midslope attenuator system. Rockfall mitigation will require difficult access techniques to reach the full height of the hazardous slope. Temporary protection of the facility and workers will be required. Repairs to damaged roadways, utilities or access pathways may be required. Repair of an existing small landslide slump along the access road is required. Final mitigation work will reduce rockfall risk to USCG personnel and facility. Waterfront structures and vessel haul-out: The waterfront structures require repairs and upgrades. Replacement of the existing floating docks is required; they will retain their current configuration (footprint) but utilize updated material specifications. Existing timber and steel piles will be either replaced, or reused with new floats, as part of this contract, depending on current condition. Geotechnical, civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical scope is included. Constraints include: Float A to be retained; guide piles at floating docks #2 and #4 to be replaced; wave screens to be replaced; electrical equipment to be upgraded; existing vessel haul-out facility to be replaced. Eel grass and SAV surveys are required to inform design. Dock operations are to be maintained during construction, per phasing to be outlined by the government. Coastal Resilience and Sedimentation Remediation: Due to the catastrophic loss of the protective coastal dune, the facility requires a comprehensive permanent solution to control massive sediment migration. Bathymetric surveys, geotechnical testing, and coastal modeling are required to inform viable design and permit alternatives. The design will utilize modern, resilient coastal engineering practices including Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), dynamic revetments, segmented offshore breakwaters/sills, and the beneficial reuse of dredged sediment wherever practicable. Construction may be implemented in functional phases to optimize funding and operational readiness. Shoreline protection repairs and upgrades are considered part of this category along with the Haul Out structure. Interim repair work: Interim repair work may be required on existing structures before new design and construction activity can be completed. If the need arises, USACE will provide USCG a description of the recommended repairs and a cost estimate. If USCG would like USACE to institute repairs, an updated agreement to define the scope will be established. 4. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically via MSForms (link is here https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Aivta2iThu) for answers to Section 3 Questions above and via email with supporting documentation requested here in Section 4 Submission Instructions. Submit your email with SUBJECT: "Response to questions on Cape Disappointment". What is the interest in submitting a proposal for a Progressive Design Build contract. Provide benefits and risks for Progressive Design Build for any of the scope items presented. What issues do you see with soliciting for construction contracts work as described in section 3. List the capabilities of your firm to do the design and construction of new segmented breakwater and haul structure working close to a Federal Channel, complex tidal currents and wave loading, complex movement of sand, and subject to large storm event What are the capabilities to design and construction for the renovation of new dock work. Do you have experience designing to USACE and/or USCG waterfront design criteria: USCG Configuration Standard Technical Orders relevant to this project scope UFC/USACE requirements relevant to this project scope Design for complex hydro loading conditions in shallow bays to USACE/UFC criteria. List previous design build work for doing work in complex environment where one had to consider the working close to a Federal Channel, complex tidal currents, complex movement of sand, subject to large storm events and is highly dynamic. List previous design build work for dock work. What issues do you see with the work. What issue do you see with design bid build. description: El Documento Europeo Único de Contratación (DEUC) consiste en una declaración responsable de la situación financiera, las capacidades, los conflictos de intereses y la idoneidad de las empresas para un procedimiento de contratación pública, conforme a un formulario normalizado. Este documento suplirá en la fase de licitación la documentación relativa a capacidad de obrar, personalidad, representación, no está incurso en las prohibiciones para contratar ni en conflictos de intereses y solvencia económica, financiera y técnica de acuerdo a lo establecido en el segundo párrafo del art. 140.1 a) de la LCSP. En el anuncio de licitación se adjuntará un archivo con formato XML común para todos los lotes con los datos del presente procedimiento de contratación que podrá importarse desde dicha web para facilitar su cumplimentación. En la siguiente dirección la Comisión Europea proporciona un servicio gratuito a los licitadores para cumplimentar en línea el formulario: https://ec.europa.eu/growth/tools-databases/espd/filter?lang=es Dicho documento se puede obtener también en formato PDF adjunto a los anuncios de licitación, a partir del Anexo II del Reglamento de Ejecución (UE) 2016/7 de la Comisión de 5 de enero de 2016, en el que constan las instrucciones para su cumplimentación, y en la dirección siguiente: https://www.boe.es/doue/2016/003/L00016-00034.pdf El DEUC cumplimentado debe firmarse con firma digital y subirse a la PLACSP. Será obligatorio indicar expresamente el lote al que se presenta la oferta. Asimismo, será obligatorio incluir un correo electrónico, a fin de poder tener un medio alternativo de notificación con carácter supletorio respecto a la PLACSP. Cuando varios empresarios y/o empresarias concurran agrupados en una unión temporal, cada una de las empresas agrupadas en la unión deberá aportar un DEUC. Si la empresa licitadora fuera a recurrir a la solvencia y medios de otras empresas para la ejecución del contrato, estas últimas también deberán presentar un DEUC en el que figure la información pertinente para estos casos. Si va a subcontratar la ejecución parcial de las prestaciones del contrato, deberá responder afirmativamente en la sección correspondiente del DEUC.
